question: Which 4.100.108 functions implement the NuttX VFS wrappers needed for file I/O (ioctl, unlink, rename)?
prototype_hypothesis: ioctl(fd, cmd, arg) dispatches the fd's driver ioctl handler; unlink(path) and rename(old, new) resolve the path and dispatch the inode unlink/rename operations. All three return NuttX status codes (negative errno).
callsite_evidence: sub_C341B98 (candidate ioctl) decompiles to the canonical NuttX fs_ioctl dispatch and references "../../nuttx/fs/vfs/fs_ioctl.c" line 52; it handles the standard command set (771 FIONBIO, 778 FIONREAD, 779 FIONWRITE, 780 FIONSPACE, 786 FIOCLEX, 787 FIONCLEX, 788 FIONBIO2, 790 FIOCNOTIFY, 791 FIOGETOWN, 1295/1296 special), returning -25 (ENOTTY) for unsupported commands

sub_C33CAF8 (candidate unlink) decompiles to the NuttX fs_unlink state machine and references "../../nuttx/fs/vfs/fs_unlink.c" line 84; it dispatches on inode type (0x442 mask over the type bits), returns -38 (ENOSYS) for missing unlink op, -39 (ENOTDIR) for a non-directory with children

sub_C33D6C4 (candidate rename) decompiles to the NuttX fs_rename path and references "../../nuttx/fs/vfs/fs_rename.c" line 534; it resolves both paths, checks directory types, dispatches the inode rename op (offset 100/104) and returns -38 (ENOSYS) when the op is absent
All three candidates were produced by the multi-layer matcher from the verified 3.101.036 symbol set and confirmed by decompiling the exact 4.100.108 IDB
The three functions are called exclusively from the file-descriptor dispatch layer and NuttX syscall handlers, matching the expected VFS wrapper call graph
control_flow_evidence: Each function uses the NuttX fd/inode resolution helper (sub_C8C8BA4, the file_get/fs_resolve equivalent) before touching the inode table
ioctl returns -25 for unknown commands and routes 1295/1296 (FIOCLEX/FIONCLEX family) through the inode-specific handler at offset 20 of the driver ops
unlink releases the inode (sub_C338200) and applies the inode-tree lock (sub_C33270C / sub_C332C5C / sub_C332C6C) around mutation
rename validates both source and destination are non-empty, resolves the destination path, and dispatches through the inode ops table (offsets 100/104), falling back to -38 (ENOSYS)
ownership_analysis: These are NuttX kernel VFS wrappers: callers own the fd/path lifetime, and the wrappers own the inode reference during the call. They must run in a context where NuttX's fd table and inode tree are valid (target-private thread, not a bare constructor).
unsafe_assumptions: The exact inode ops offsets (88/100/104, 24/44) are BES1503 NuttX layout specifics recovered from this IDB and must not be assumed identical on other targets
ioctl's variadic argument handling (a3 as va_list) requires the caller to pass a pointer-compatible argument, not an integer promoted through a register that the wrapper then dereferences incorrectly
recommended_probe: Open a device file, issue ioctl/unlink/rename via the target-private facade, and confirm the returned status matches the NuttX expected errno for each command and error path.
